title: Faith, Hope, and Charity, These Three
description: Faith, Hope, and Charity, These Three in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 388 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Christian Graces”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Faith, hope, and char-i-ty, these three, Yet is the great-est char-i-ty; Fa-ther of lights, these gifts im-part To mine and ev-ery hu-man heart.

lines: Faith, hope, and charity, these three,
Father of lights, these gifts impart
To mine and every human heart.
Faith, that in prayer can never fail,
Hope, that o'er doubting must prevail,
Is God's own name, for God is love.
The morning star is lost in light,
The rainbow passes with the storm
And hope with sorrow's fading form.
Beyond the reach of death and time,
Like the blue sky's all-bounding space,
Holds heaven and earth in its embrace.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
